title.en: AN ACT DEFINING THE JURISDICTION OF THE CIVIL AND OF THE MILITARY AUTHORITIES OVER LANDS RESERVED BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES FOR MILITARY
title.orig: AN ACT DEFINING THE JURISDICTION OF THE CIVIL AND OF THE MILITARY AUTHORITIES OVER LANDS RESERVED BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES FOR MILITARY

source.name: The LawPhil Project — Arellano Law Foundation

completenessNote: 全文，共 10 条；逐字取自 LawPhil PDF 文本化成果（第三方 OCR，非机翻），原始文件 ACT_00530_1902_html.txt

text.en:
No licenses shall be granted for the sale of or dealing in any intoxicating liquors on any public
land reserved by the President of the United States for military purposes in the Philippine Islands.

The military authorities shall have the right to reject any intruder or trespasser on any public lands
reserved by the President for military purposes in the Philippine Islands, and to suppress open broaches of
the peace and abate nuisances thereon.

No branch of the Civil Government in force on or over any public lands reserved by the President
for military purposes, and an civilian residents thereon, shall interfere with military administration or the use
of such lands for military purposes.

The personal property of persons employed in the military service of the United States in the
Philippine Islands and used by them incident to said service shall be exempt from all taxation under the laws
in force in said Islands.

No mining claims shall be located by any person on any public lands reserved by the President for
military purposes in the Philippine Islands.

Every person who unlawfully cuts, or aids, or is employed in unlawfully cutting, or wantonly
destroys, or procures to be wantonly destroyed, any timber standing upon lands of the United States, which
in pursuance of law may be reserved or purchased for military purposes in the Philippine Islands, or removes
any other public property, shall, upon conviction, be fined for each offense a sum not exceeding five hundred
dollars, or be imprisoned for a period not exceeding twelve months, or both, in the discretion of the court.

No arrest of any officer, soldier, or civilian employee, in the military service of the United States
on any military reservation, camp, or barracks, shall be made except on warrant in due form in writing and
served upon the commanding officer thereof.

All laws or parts of laws in force in the Philippine Islands not inconsistent with military use of any
public lands reserved by the President for military purposes shall be in full force and effect over said lands.

The public good requiring the speedy enactment of this bill, the passage of the same is hereby
expedited in accordance with section two of "An Act prescribing the order of procedure by the Commission
in the enactment of laws," passed September twenty-sixth, nineteen hundred.

This Act shall take effort on its passage.
Enacted, November 24, 1902.
